messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High GPU queue growth observed for inference-cluster-prod. queue_length=8.2k, tail_latency_p95=3.4s, error_rate=6.8% :rotating_light:

Devon (oncall): seeing this — thanks for the page. I’m joining. Any immediate customer reports? @Customer Success - Priya

Customer Success - Priya: 2 customers reported increased latencies in the last 10m, one reported requests timing out. No cancellation tickets yet but CS is standing by.

Alex P.: logs show cluster-autoscaler failing to create nodes: "LaunchTemplateVersionMismatch: requested version not found" and also a PassRole error in cloud provider. Snippet from cloud: 
```
ERROR: AttachRolePolicyDenied: arn:aws:iam::123456:role/redwood-node-role cannot be assumed by ec2:PassRole
```

Maria G.: ugh. we just rolled a launch template update in us-west-2 earlier today. autoscaler might be hitting the old nodegroup config. CA events: scale up attempted 24 times, failed due to ASG error 400.

Devon (oncall): what's the immediate mitigation? Can we spin a temporary nodegroup with a known-good LT and instance profile?

Alex P.: yes — two options: 1) create an emergency nodegroup with the previous working launch-template version + correct instance profile, or 2) patch the ASG/launchtemplate so CA can attach. Given time pressure, option 1 is faster. I can run the ASG create. Need approval to bump capacity and run emergency nodes.

Tilly S.: +1 for emergency nodegroup. Also we should consider removing the taint on the existing nodegroup if taint propagation is blocking scheduling, but I think schedule failures are due to not enough nodes rather than taints.

Devon (oncall): go ahead, Alex. Make it single AZ to avoid extra quotas. Notify infra if you need extra quotas.

Alex P.: creating nodegroup now. Command: 
```bash
aws eks create-nodegroup --cluster-name inference-cluster-prod --nodegroup-name emergency-gpu-2471 --scaling-config minSize=0,maxSize=10,desiredSize=4 --instance-types p3.8xlarge --launch-template name=redwood-gpu-lt,version=12 --node-role arn:aws:iam::123456:role/redwood-node-role --subnets subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb --labels emergency=true
```

infra-bot: ASG quota check: allowed. creating ASG and nodegroup.

Alex P.: nodegroup creation started. Meanwhile, we should also patch CA tolerations if any pods are stuck pending due to taints. Running: 
```bash
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending
```

Maria G.: observed many pods in Pending with message "0/45 nodes are available: 45 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu". So it's capacity not taints. Good.

Devon (oncall): ok, primary mitigation=emergency nodes. Secondary: rollback launch template change in staging then prod, but that’s heavier. Also start throttling non-critical jobs. Can we mark inference-batch-queue as lower priority?

Alex P.: I added a temporary Autoscale annotation to the inference batch deployment to set maxReplicas=2 and paused its scheduler: 
```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    redwood.com/pause-scaling: "true"
```
This should reduce background GPU churn.

incident-bot: update: emergency nodegroup creation succeeded, instances provisioning (EC2 pending) — expected join 3-8m.

Devon (oncall): monitoring queue length. Maria, what's tail latency and 429/503 ratio?

Maria G.: tail_latency_p95 peaked at 3.8s, now stabilizing at 3.1s. 503s rose from 0.2% to 6.8%. After pause of batch jobs, 503s down to 4.1% and queue growth slowed.

Tilly S.: we should notify impacted customers and give ETA for mitigation. Priya?

Customer Success - Priya: messaging ready, will send advisory to impacted customers: "We are provisioning emergency GPU capacity; expected recovery within 15-25 minutes. We will follow up with a formal incident report."

Alex P.: nodes are joining: 2/4 Ready. Kubelet logs show kubelet registering and pulling device plugin. Starting to schedule pods onto new nodes.

Devon (oncall): good. Any blocking error while scheduling?

Maria G.: a subset of pods had nodeSelector mismatch due to an unexpected label on the nodegroup (we used label 'emergency=true' but some deployments require 'accelerator=gpu'). Patching deployments now to accept emergency nodes.

Alex P.: patched deployments to accept both labels. Re-triggering pending pods.

incident-bot: Scheduling progress: pending pods -> running 180/260 (69%) after nodes joined. Queue length dropping from 8.2k -> 4.6k.

Devon (oncall): good. keep pressure on autoscaler fix afterwards. This is a mitigation. Who will own the rollback/launch-template fix?

Maria G.: I’ll own the LT rollback and IAM PassRole root cause. Early hypothesis: new LT referenced an instance profile that lacked the PassRole trust or we uploaded an invalid IAM policy during rollout. I’ll open a ticket to infra and include logs.

Tilly S.: also check cluster-autoscaler permissions — CA needs to be able to describe and set ASG sizes and create instances. If role changes were made, CA could be blocked.

Alex P.: nodes now at desired 4, pod scheduling at 240/260 (92%), queue at 2.1k. Customer error rate down to 1.3%.

Devon (oncall): excellent. Prioritize the follow-ups: 
- Maria: LT rollback + IAM fix + test in staging (owner)
- Tilly: CA permissions audit & add extra observability for LT mismatches (owner)
- Alex: document the emergency nodegroup procedure and small runbook for single-AZ emergency provisioning (owner)
- Priya/CS: customer updates and post-incident follow-up (owner)

Customer Success - Priya: Sent update to customers: "We’ve provisioned emergency capacity; most traffic normalized. We’ll share root cause and remediation timeline in the incident report."

Devon (oncall): setting incident severity to SEV-2 and creating incident issue. We’ll keep channel open for 30m for stabilization. Reassign to SRE rotation for full RCA.

incident-bot: note: please file incident ticket at /incidents/2471112223 and tag with #gpu-provisioning #autoscaler #iam

Alex P.: quick follow-up: when I created the nodegroup I used launch-template version 12 which matched last known good. We should add a pre-flight validation check to the deploy pipeline to ensure new LT version is compatible with CA.

Maria G.: agreed. I’ll add a validation step: ensure instanceProfile and passRole permissions are present, and test ASG create in staging.

Devon (oncall): thanks all. If anyone sees regression, alert immediately. I’m handing off to SRE morning shift in 25m.

Tilly S.: leaving a note: postmortem to include why the rollout was allowed to proceed without CA/ASG compatibility checks and whether the rollout should have blocked if PassRole failed.

incident-bot: thread closed for now; reopen if issues reappear.

Devon (oncall): closing channel for active mitigation. Follow-up doc will be posted to #postmortems and linked from the incident ticket."
